baez_const.source: J. C. Baez, The Fundamental Theorem of Natural Selection, arXiv:2107.05610v3 [q-bio.PE], 6 Oct 2021, p. 4 (Section 2)
baez_const.text: The second term of equation (5) only vanishes in special cases, e.g. when the fitness functions f_i are constant. When the second term vanishes we have d f-bar/dt = Var(f). This is a satisfying result. It says the mean fitness does not decrease, and it increases whenever some replicators are more fit than others, at a rate equal to the variance in fitness.

baez_ewens.source: J. C. Baez, arXiv:2107.05610v3, p. 1 and p. 2
baez_ewens.text: Some tried to make this statement precise as follows: The time derivative of the mean fitness of a population equals the variance of its fitness. But this is only true under very restrictive conditions, so a controversy was ignited. [p. 1]. ... Ewens concluded that 'the theorem does not provide the substantial biological statement that Fisher claimed'. [p. 2]

lagatta_price72.text: In Price's view, 'The main cause of misunderstanding about the theorem is that everyone has supposed that Fisher was talking about the total change rather than just the fraction of this due to natural selection' [Pri72a, p. 130].
